name: Diversity-engineered synthetic crowd: internal LMSR, wagering, meta-prediction and information-partitioned Delphi panels
one_line: Aggregate LLM agents that differ by model family and evidence shard through an internal market, wagers or peer prediction and pass the gated gap to the price to a stacker; unproven: on 574 resolved Polymarket question-rounds five families' errors correlate 0.70 within outcome (N_eff ~1.3), their mean loses to the price by 0.064 Brier and a blend with the price adds nothing.
maturity: Experimental; no mechanism scored against a price; InfoDelphi +12-18% over LLM baselines without a price benchmark; lab monoculture evidence on TruthfulQA; nobody trading it
requires_ai: yes; LLM agents give beliefs, peer / price predictions, wagers
edge: Hypothetical: decorrelated agents plus market-style weighting add information the price lacks
capital: <$1k-$10k after validation; file 21 sizing, LLM spend binds
build_time: 2-3 weeks on top of file 21's harness
opportunity_size: A fraction of file 21's long-tail pool; zero measured addition over the price; 21,856 post-cutoff resolved markets to test on
expected_results: no public data, theoretical only; guess 0-0.003 Brier over file 21, PnL negative after LLM costs
competition: research code and hobby swarms; no live record; cross-family ensembles already standard
flag: none specific; geoblock / close-only and data clause (E9)
validate: Replay on 900-1,400 post-cutoff mid-band markets; kill if internal market = logistic aggregator or blend = mid
top_risk: Monoculture: cross-family errors correlate 0.70 even with outcome removed
solo_fit_reason: Cheap to test on top of file 21 (every arm reuses one set of calls, and ForecastBench's free forecasts already let a solo developer measure correlation and aggregator gains offline), but the own measurement found five model families worth ~1.3 independent forecasters, a logistic stacker worse than the plain mean out of sample, and no gain from blending the crowd into the price; the LLM bill (~$0.55 per question) exceeds any plausible edge below ~$10k deployed.
speed_class: speed-insensitive: 12-call crowd per market; skill exists only at listing
results_10k: as file 21 plus crowd feature; -$800 to +$50/month (guess)
capacity_ceiling: file 21's ~$15-30k; the crowd adds accuracy at best, not capacity
services: historical order books (own recorder or Telonex)
changes_made: Written 2026-09-29 as the merged 'diversity-engineered synthetic crowd' file per both critic notes: internal LMSR with wealth dynamics, WALLA wagering, meta-prediction (peer prediction, surprisingly popular, knowledgeable-dissent filter) and the absorbed information-partitioned Delphi panel (incl. the OSINT-sensor variant), one shared ablation harness (rho = 1.0 control, plain logistic aggregator, independent vote); boundaries with files 21, 56, 57, 58, 62 stated.

Own baseline 1 (ForecastBench processed forecast sets, CC BY-SA 4.0, 18 rounds 2025-10-26 to 2026-06-21, 1,941 resolved market question-rounds): five model families on 574 Polymarket question-rounds, error correlation 0.907 raw and 0.70-0.71 within outcome (N_eff 1.08 / 1.30); same-family pairs 0.49-0.80 vs cross-family 0.60-0.78; mean 0.144 vs market 0.079; walk-forward logistic stacker worse than the mean (+0.015); blend with the price +0.002 (n.s.); power SDs 0.036 / 0.049-0.053 (blend vs market) and ~0.10 (aggregator vs aggregator).

Own baseline 2: Nous's released outputs recomputed (10 persona agents of one model on 42 Polymarket questions: error correlation 0.984, N_eff 1.01); PolyBench's per-model dataset checked but login-gated (OneDrive 403 / 401).

Own baseline 3: Gamma per-tag keyset pull of markets listed and closed in 2026 (21,856 resolved binaries >= $5k volume in 5,855 events, plus 49,073 weather buckets) and CLOB prices-history on 365 markets (one per event): market Brier 0.179 / 0.110 / 0.071 at listing + 1 day / T-7d / T-1d on 321 / 315 / 315 markets with 118 / 106 / 103 Yes; live books on 40 mid-band non-sports markets (median spread 2.5c below $10k liquidity, 1.0c above; $127-298 vs $1.4-1.6k within 5c).

Adjacent field fetched and corrected against the brief: Begin et al. is TruthfulQA with 7-9B models and role diversity did cut rho (0.60 -> 0.44); WALLA's forecasting test is a synthetic set it built and it lands slightly below centralised stacking; Douven's market is Manifold (play money) and the 23% is on 94 clean items; InfoDelphi uses one model and cuts evidence at the resolution date with no price benchmark; Nous's r ~0.77 is a quoted external figure; added Beygelzimer-Langford-Pennock (Kelly-bettor market = wealth-weighted Bayes pool, so the internal LMSR is computed in closed form), Nechepurenko & Shuvalov (100 post-cutoff Polymarket markets, best design 0.153 vs market 0.152), Pnyx (LMSR farther from the Bayes posterior than static pools, persistent bankrolls hurt).

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-29 (29 numbered sources re-fetched or re-queried: 25 arXiv abstracts / HTML incl. arXiv API metadata, Pnyx and PolyBench READMEs, ForecastBench datasets page and wiki, Polymarket fee docs, GitHub / HN searches; E7 / E8 / E9 passages; fb_analyse.py, fb_corr_extra.py, nous_corr.py, replay_analyse.py and live_depth.py re-run): 29 confirmed, 5 corrected, 0 removed, 0 unreachable. Material corrections: (1) power re-derived on the paired Brier difference and made honest about blend weight: the fitted blend put ~5% logit weight on the crowd; at a 20% weight the mid-band paired SD is 0.068, so a 0.005 gain needs ~1,400 questions (not 415-880) and Phase 1 is resized to 900-1,400 mid-band questions and ~$1,100-1,700 (verifier v_power.py); (2) the replay sample's 8-days-actually-open filter is a look-ahead: 1,436 early-closing markets (Yes rate 0.38) were dropped, 72 re-pulled score 0.100 at listing + 1 day, so the ex-ante figure is ~0.17 not 0.179; CLOB prices-history is the raw midpoint and the lowest-volume third scores 0.194 vs 0.169 on the top third (v_early.py); both stated in the validation plan with the fix (filter on scheduled end, score on recorded books); (3) the lab-vs-market monoculture comparison is not like for like: Begin et al. correlate binary right / wrong vectors, here probability errors, so 'worse than the lab' became 'at least as severe'; the '0.87-0.94' after 0.91 is the range over ten pairs, not a CI; (4) ForecastBench timing checked on its wiki: forecasts are due on the due date and market_value_on_due_date is that day's value, so the price is contemporaneous (the writer's open doubt about a later price is resolved); (5) the internal-market wording now says the closed form is the Kelly-equilibrium limit of a clearing market (Beygelzimer et al.), not an LMSR; AceMAD's six benchmarks named (QA / reasoning, not forecasting); six-family correlation flagged as 22 Yes only; live depth re-snapshot added ($115-178 / $1.6-3.5k within 5c); meta-prediction evidence status added to Maturity; Phase 2 budget raised to $400-1,000. Boundaries with 21, 50, 56, 58, 62 checked: no duplication of 58's gating or 62's herd trading. 15 fields 2,493 -> 2,538 words.
open_doubts: The correlation and aggregator results use ForecastBench zero-shot forecasts (no retrieval, no price); they bound, not measure, a retrieval-fed crowd on disjoint evidence shards, which only Phase 1 can show.

The power figures come from a blend that put ~5% weight on the crowd; if a retrieval-fed crowd earns more weight the paired SD rises (0.068 at a 20% weight), so the Phase 1 size may still be short for a 0.005 gain.

Question-rounds repeat the same Polymarket question across biweekly rounds (574 rounds, 472 questions); CIs are clustered by question, but events with several related questions are not clustered together.

The replay-pool market Brier comes from CLOB raw midpoints and a sample filtered on actual close (a look-ahead, corrected only approximately from 72 re-pulled early closers); historical executable spreads are unknown.
Live depth is two same-day snapshots of 40 books from the first 4,000 keyset markets with >= $1k liquidity (an older cohort).

No test anywhere of the knowledgeable-dissent filter, the surprisingly-popular shift on LLM forecasts or WALLA on real forecasting questions; the cost per question (~$0.55) is an estimate from list prices, not a measured run.
